title: Edge shard scaling: latency & cost economics snapshot
content:
Purpose:
This is a working snapshot of a small-batch benchmark exploring two edge scaling strategies for session-oriented workloads: horizontal shard scaling (more small shards, single-session affinity) vs. vertical consolidation (fewer larger shards, multiplexing many sessions). Goal is to capture latency percentiles, slot utilization, and approximate dollars-per-1M-tokens under our current edge instance types (g4x-equivalent).

Context / why this matters:
- We are expanding the edge footprint to reduce client RTT and p50 for interactive flows.
- Edge capacity is limited and higher cost than core. Tradeoff: keep many small pinned shards (better cold/warm affinity, lower p50 for sticky sessions) vs. larger shared shards that improve GPU utilization but risk p99 spikes during microbursts.

Experiment (brief):
- Workload: conversation sessions, median turn length 28 tokens, 2.4 turns/session, 35% chance of immediate follow-up within 2s (creates microburst clustering).
- Model: quantized-8b variant used for edge tests.
- Instance: edge-small-g (8 vCPU, 24GB RAM, 1xA10-like), baseline config for both strategies.
- Duration: continuous 6h runs, three independent runs per strategy (different seeds).
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99 generation latency (ms), slot fill % (average GPU utilization proxy), requests/second, tail frequency of queuing events, approximated infra cost ($) normalized per 1M tokens served.
- Routing: deterministic — sessions pinned to a shard for the duration for horizontal strategy; vertical shards accept any session for consolidation strategy with session stickiness TTL=30s for cache hits.

Results (aggregated median across runs):

ASCII Table: latency & cost summary per strategy

Strategy             | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | slot_fill % | req/s | $ / 1M tokens
---------------------|----------|----------|----------|-------------|-------|---------------
Horizontal (many)    |  72      |  165     |  420     |  38         |  85   |  68.3         
Vertical (consol)    |  88      |  190     |  720     |  67         |  150  |  43.9         

Observations (raw):
- p50: horizontal wins (~18ms lower) because session-local KV/cache warm starts reduce generation setup cost.
- p99: vertical consolidation shows substantially worse tails (720ms) vs horizontal (420ms) driven by queue buildup during microbursts and larger multiplex windows.
- Slot_fill %: consolidation improves utilization (67% vs 38%), which explains lower cost-per-token for vertical strategy.
- Req/s throughput significantly higher for vertical due to packing efficiency and reduced per-session per-shard overhead.

Microprofile breakdown (typical burst vs sustained):
- Sustained 60% arrival rate: vertical keeps p90 within 210ms; horizontal remains stable but underutilized.
- Microburst pattern (100 reqs in 3s within pinned sessions): horizontal absorbs bursts with minimal queueing (p90 spike +30%), vertical shows queueing that pushes p99 above 1s in worst runs.

Interpretation / tradeoffs:
- Cost vs latency tail: consolidation is ~36% cheaper per token but has ~70% worse p99 latency. For interactive apps where occasional sub-second tails are tolerated, vertical is attractive. For tightly SLA'd chat (p99 < 500ms), horizontal approach is preferable despite higher unit costs.
- Predictability: horizontal provides more predictable tail behavior for sticky sessions; vertical requires more robust admission or dynamic prioritization logic to protect percentiles.
- Observability/rollout: consolidation needs better microburst detection and fast preemption/fallback to avoid long p99s.

Recommendations (next experiments / product levers to evaluate):
1) Hybrid shard sizing: test a middle-ground where 60% of traffic goes to consolidated pool and 40% to pinned shards (session-duration-aware routing). Measure incremental p99 improvement and cost delta.
2) Fast fallback: implement admission-based fallback where a vertical shard can opt to return a lightweight fallback (smaller model or cached stub) when queue depth > threshold. Run A/B to measure user-visible quality loss vs cost saved.
3) Prefetch + KV cache TTL tuning: horizontal relies on short pre-warm TTL; sweep TTL in {15s,30s,120s} to find sweet spot for local cache hit rate vs memory overhead.
4) SLO-aware autoscale on-edge: evaluate microburst headroom reservations (min spare slots) vs cost of idle capacity.

Operational notes (open questions & TODOs):
- TODO: capture energy-per-token on these edge instance types; ask infra for power profiling (ticket JIRA-PE-4190).
- Open: rate of model quantization-induced variance — runs used quant-8b; verify with quant-6b for consolidation since smaller models may change p99 shape.
- TODO: run the hybrid routing above for at least 24h continuous to observe diurnal pattern impacts (assign to Riley).
- Question: do we consider per-customer isolation rules that force horizontal for enterprise customers paying for p99 SLAs? If so, we need pricing tier mapping.

Proposed playbook snippet (if we choose consolidation-by-default):
- Default: vertical consolidated shards for free-tier + mid-tier customers (lower unit costs).
- Enterprise SLA: reserve pinned shards or higher priority admission paths (charge premium).
- Protect: implement microburst circuit that triggers temporary additional shards or shed to fallback model to keep p99 < 1s.

Appendix: quick synthetic time series example (one run excerpt, vertical strategy)
- t=00:00–00:30: steady 120 req/s -> p99 ~ 210ms
- t=00:31: microburst cluster (300 reqs in 2s) -> queue depth spikes, p99 jump to 980ms for ~6s -> then tail decays over 18s back to baseline.
- Cost note: cost estimate uses on-demand pricing equivalent and amortizes infra over tokens observed; does not include network egress or storage.

Questions for reviewers:
- Are these assumptions for session stickiness aligned with product telemetry? (we guessed 35% follow-up probability)
- Which SLA bands should we hard-qualify for pinned-shards by default?
- Any objections to a 2-arm rollout for hybrid routing next week?
